name: Khuga Dam
description: Multipurpose dam on the Khuga (Tuitha) River south of Churachandpur town, inaugurated in 2010. Popular picnic and viewpoint spot with reservoir, hills, and scenic surroundings.
facts: Height 38 m, length about 230 m
Construction started 1983, resumed 2002, inaugurated by Sonia Gandhi in 2010
Located near Mata village, about 7-10 km south of Churachandpur town
Also known as Tuitha or Mata Dam
Popular for local picnics and photography

name: Ngaloi Waterfall
description: Cascading waterfall near Ngaloi (Ngaloimoul) village, about 9 km from Churachandpur. Surrounded by low hills and greenery, a popular accessible nature spot.
facts: Located at Ngaloimoul village on Tipaimukh Road
About 9 km from Churachandpur town
Funded under Manipur Tourism; short access path
Best during or after monsoon for fuller flow
Also called Ngaloimoul Falls

name: Tonglon Caves
description: Historic limestone caves in Singngat sub-division featuring carvings, sculptures, and engravings linked to early settlements and tribal history.
facts: Most famous caves of Churachandpur district
Located in Singngat area, roughly 10-32 km from town depending on route
Carvings provide insight into early human settlements
Archaeological and cultural significance
Access involves some trekking

name: Tuibuong Tribal Museum
description: Ethnographic museum in Churachandpur town (Tuibuong/Tedim Road area) showcasing artifacts, traditional attire, tools, and cultural heritage of local Kuki-Chin-Mizo tribes.
facts: Located on Tedim Road in Churachandpur town
Displays costumes, arms, relics, and historical documents of hill tribes
Also known as Zogam or Hill Community Tribal Museum in some sources
Provides insight into early settlements and tribal lifestyles

name: Churachandpur Town
description: District headquarters and second-largest town in Manipur, locally called Lamka. Gateway to southern hills with vibrant tribal markets, handicrafts, and base for exploring nearby nature spots.
facts: Locally known as Lamka; named after Maharaja Churachand Singh
About 60-65 km southwest of Imphal on Tedim Road (NH-2)
Hub for Kuki, Paite, Hmar, Zou and other tribal communities
Famous for traditional handicrafts, weaving, and bamboo work
Elevation around 800-900 m

name: Lunjang Waterfall
description: Remote cascading waterfall in the hills near Pamzal/Lunjang village, deeper into the forested areas of Churachandpur, offering a more secluded nature experience.
facts: Located near Pamzal or Lunjang Behiang area
About 20-25 km from Churachandpur town; requires trek of 30-45 min
Less visited than Ngaloi; part of Pamzal Reserved Forest zone
Best after rains for fuller cascade

name: Suangdoh Village
description: Traditional tribal village in Churachandpur district offering glimpses of local Kuki-Chin culture, lifestyle, and rural hill life.
facts: Cultural site showcasing indigenous traditions
Part of the broader tribal landscape of the district
Access from Churachandpur town

name: Pamzal Reserved Forest
description: Dense sub-tropical reserved forest area around Pamzal with waterfalls, biodiversity, and opportunities for nature walks and birdwatching.
facts: Critical ecological zone with evergreen and semi-evergreen forests
Contains several waterfalls including Step's and Pipeline
Home to local flora and fauna
Access via Pamzal village
